power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

stat_p_nonsig.report: Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is 'no effect', 'no difference', or that groups are 'the same' after p > 0.05. It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. text.text: Persistent methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) bacteraemia is associated with significant morbidity and mortality.
Cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy has demonstrated synergistic activity in preclinical models and small case series, but comparative clinical evidence is lacking.
We conducted a multicentre retrospective review of all patients aged ≥18 years with persistent MSSA bacteraemia at two Queensland tertiary hospitals between January 2014 and December 2024.

The primary outcome was time to blood culture sterilisation, compared between patients who commenced cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy prior to first negative blood culture and a matched cohort of non-combination-treated patients.
Secondary outcomes included 90-day all-cause mortality, 90-day relapse, development of multi-resistant organisms, Clostridioides difficile infection, and adverse drug events.
A total of 288 episodes of persistent MSSA bacteraemia in 283 patients were identified.
Twenty-six patients received cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy.

Among the 14 patients who commenced combination therapy prior to first negative blood culture, median time to sterilisation was 1 day (IQR 1-2), compared with 2 days (IQR 1-3) in the matched non-combination group.
Cox regression in the matched cohort (n=114) demonstrated an increased rate of blood culture clearance with combination therapy (HR 1.8; 95% CI 1.2-2.7; P =0.004).
In the full cohort, ninety-day mortality (20.0% vs 23.0%, P=0.73) and relapse rates (11.5% vs 8.3%, P =0.57) did not differ significantly between groups.
Cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy was associated with accelerated blood culture sterilisation in persistent MSSA bacteraemia.
Prospective randomised evaluation is warranted.

Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia (SAB) is a leading cause of infectious mortality worldwide, affecting more than one million patients annually with a 90-day all-cause mortality ranging from 15-30%. [1, 2] Optimal management requires early initiation of effective antibiotic therapy, source control, and infectious diseases consultation. [2] Among patients with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA) bacteraemia, cefazolin has emerged as the preferred beta-lactam agent, offering comparable efficacy to anti-staphylococcal penicillins with a more favourable tolerability profile, including lower rates of acute kidney injury. [3] [4] [5] Despite best-practice management, approximately 15 -30% of patients develop persistent bacteraemia, defined as ongoing bacteraemia for ≥72 hours despite appropriate therapies [2, 6] Persistent SAB carries a disproportionate mortality burden, with each additional day of bacteraemia estimated to increase 30-day mortality risk by approximately 16%. [7] There is no established standard of care for refractory MSSA bacteraemia beyond optimised dosing and source control. [2] A specific concern with cefazolin in deep seated infection is the inoculum effect, mediated by expression of the blaZ gene, which can attenuate bactericidal activity at the bacterial burdens encountered in endocarditis, epidural abscess, and persistent bacteraemia. [8, 9] Combination antibiotic strategies have been explored as a means to accelerate bacteraemia clearance in SAB.
text.formatted: Staphylococcus aureus bacteraemia (SAB) is a leading cause of infectious mortality worldwide, affecting more than one million patients annually with a 90-day all-cause mortality ranging from 15-30%. <ref type="bibr" target="#b0">[1,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b1">2]</ref> Optimal management requires early initiation of effective antibiotic therapy, source control, and infectious diseases consultation. <ref type="bibr" target="#b1">[2]</ref> Among patients with methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA) bacteraemia, cefazolin has emerged as the preferred beta-lactam agent, offering comparable efficacy to anti-staphylococcal penicillins with a more favourable tolerability profile, including lower rates of acute kidney injury. <ref type="bibr" target="#b2">[3]</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b3">[4]</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b4">[5]</ref> Despite best-practice management, approximately 15 -30% of patients develop persistent bacteraemia, defined as ongoing bacteraemia for ≥72 hours despite appropriate therapies <ref type="bibr" target="#b1">[2,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b5">6]</ref> Persistent SAB carries a disproportionate mortality burden, with each additional day of bacteraemia estimated to increase 30-day mortality risk by approximately 16%. <ref type="bibr" target="#b6">[7]</ref> There is no established standard of care for refractory MSSA bacteraemia beyond optimised dosing and source control. <ref type="bibr" target="#b1">[2]</ref> A specific concern with cefazolin in deep seated infection is the inoculum effect, mediated by expression of the blaZ gene, which can attenuate bactericidal activity at the bacterial burdens encountered in endocarditis, epidural abscess, and persistent bacteraemia. <ref type="bibr" target="#b7">[8,</ref> <ref type="bibr" target="#b8">9]</ref> Combination antibiotic strategies have been explored as a means to accelerate bacteraemia clearance in SAB.

text.text: Adjunctive rifampicin was associated with faster bacteraemia clearance but conferred no survival benefit in the ARREST trial, and combination cloxacillinfosfomycin was stopped early for futility in the SAFO trial of MSSA bacteraemia. [10, 11] To address the challenge of persistent MSSA infection, cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy has been proposed as a salvage strategy.

text.text: The combination exploits complementary binding affinity for distinct penicillin-binding proteins: cefazolin predominantly targets penicillin binding protein 2 (PBP2) while ertapenem has strong affinity for penicillin binding protein 1 (PBP1), together enhancing bactericidal activity in high-burden infections. [12] In vitro synergy has been demonstrated across multiple assay platforms, and further evidence suggests the combination may enhance host immune clearance through immunomodulatory mechanisms, including stimulation of interleukin-1β release from peripheral blood mononuclear cells. [9, [13] [14] [15] Rapid blood culture sterilisation following cefazolin-ertapenem salvage therapy has been reported in five small case series of patients with persistent MSSA bacteraemia, including patients with endocarditis and central nervous system (CNS) metastatic disease. [9, 13, [15] [16] [17] Across these case series, a total of 70 patients have received beta-lactam-ertapenem combination therapy for persistent MSSA bacteraemia or endocarditis, including 57 treated specifically with cefazolin-ertapenem; however, no matched comparative analysis has been performed. [9, 13, [15] [16] [17] We therefore conducted a multicentre retrospective cohort study of cefazolin-ertapenem as salvage treatment for persistent MSSA bacteraemia across two Queensland tertiary centres over a ten-year period.

text.text: This multicentre retrospective observational study was conducted at two tertiary hospitals in Queensland, Australia: The Prince Charles Hospital (TPCH) and the Royal Brisbane and Women's Hospital (RBWH).
We included all patients aged ≥18 years with MSSA bacteraemia of ≥72 hours duration between January 2014 and December 2024.
Exclusion criteria were: bacteraemia duration less than 72 hours, polymicrobial bacteraemia, and MRSA as the causative organism.
Cases were identified from AUSLAB (PJA Solutions Pty Ltd, Pathology Queensland), which captures all pathology tests ordered from public health facilities in Queensland.
Clinical data including comorbidities, antibiotic therapy, and imaging were retrieved from patient records.

Ninety-day vital status (alive or deceased) and clinical follow-up were verified through the hospital medical record and Queensland Health's state-wide clinical information systems, which provide cross-facility admission records and linkage to mortality data for patients managed within the Queensland public health system.
Ethics approval was granted by the Metro North Health Human Research Ethics Committee (HREC/2025/MNH/11558).
Persistent MSSA bacteraemia was defined as ≥72 hours of positive cultures.[ 2] Episodes occurring ≥90 days apart were recorded as separate events.

Relapse was defined as a positive MSSA blood culture after 72 hours of negativity with new or worsening symptoms within 90 days. [18, 19] Comorbidity was assessed using the Charlson Comorbidity Index (CCI). [20]

text.text: The primary outcome was time to first negative blood culture from the index date.
For patients receiving cefazolin-ertapenem "combination therapy", the index date was the date combination therapy was commenced.
For comparator patients (described below), the index date was the corresponding matched day of bacteraemia.

Secondary outcomes included 90day all-cause mortality, 90-day MSSA relapse, development of antimicrobial-resistant organisms, Clostridioides difficile infection, and adverse drug events ([ADE], captured across the entire admission).
Follow-up was defined as time from the index date until death or 90 days, whichever occurred first.
The primary analysis included patients who commenced combination therapy before the date of their first negative blood culture.
Patients in whom clearance coincided with the index date were excluded, as the temporal relationship between treatment commencement and microbiological response could not be reliably established.
A sensitivity analysis retaining these patients was also performed.

For each combination-treated patient included in the primary analysis, a matched comparator set was identified comprising all patients who remained bacteraemic on the corresponding bacteremia day and who shared the same age group (<50, 50 -<70, ≥70 years), CCI category (0, 1-4, ≥5), and presence of major metastatic foci (bone/joint, cardiac, or CNS involvement).

text.text: All eligible comparators were included without a fixed matching ratio; where a comparator was eligible for more than one exposed patient, they were included once only, assigned to the risk set corresponding to the longest duration of bacteraemia.
The comparator group comprised patients receiving any regimen other than cefazolin-ertapenem, reflecting realworld practice and heterogeneity.

Patients who commenced combination therapy after their first negative blood culture remained eligible for selection as comparators, as eligibility was determined using only information available at the matched timepoint The effect of combination therapy on time to blood culture clearance was estimated using Cox proportional hazards regression with cluster-robust standard errors to account for the matched structure, with the competing risk of death accounted for in a sensitivity analysis.
Summary statistics are presented as mean (SD), median (IQR), or n (%) as appropriate; between-group comparisons used Student's t-test, Wilcoxon rank-sum, chi-square, or Fisher's exact test.
All analyses were performed in Stata (Version 19.5; StataCorp LLC). [21] A twosided P<0.05 was considered statistically significant.

text.text: In this retrospective cohort study, cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy was associated with accelerated blood culture sterilisation in patients with persistent MSSA bacteraemia, with a median time to clearance of one day from the index date compared with two days in matched comparator patients (HR 1.8; 95% CI 1.2-2.7; P=0.004).

The rapidity of sterilisation is consistent with prior case series, in which clearance within 24 hours was observed in the majority of evaluable patients. [9, 13, 15] Although each additional day of bacteraemia is estimated to increase 30-day mortality risk by approximately 16%, randomised trials of strategies that accelerate clearance have not consistently translated this association into a mortality benefit; whether cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy can do so remains an open question. [6, 22] Randomised trials of combination antibiotic therapy in SAB have demonstrated shorter bacteraemia duration without mortality benefit, a pattern observed with vancomycin-flucloxacillin in MRSA bacteraemia (CAMERA2) and cloxacillin-fosfomycin in MSSA bacteraemia (SAFO), and whether the association seen here reflects a true causal pathway or residual confounding by indication cannot be established from retrospective data. [10, 23] No significant difference in 90-day mortality was observed (20.0% vs 23.0%), though the study was not powered to detect such a difference.

text.text: This is reassuring given that combination therapy was preferentially used in the most clinically complex patients, those with significant metastatic disease, ICU-level illness, and greater comorbidity burden, in whom worse outcomes might a priori be expected, and further suggests the observed effect on clearance may be conservative.

Adverse drug reaction rates were numerically higher in the combination group, though attribution in the retrospective setting is inherently limited given the substantial overlap between manifestations of systemic sepsis and antibiotic toxicity, and the markedly greater number of concurrent antimicrobial agents received by combination-treated patients (median 6 vs 3, P<0.001). [24, 25] The median duration of combination therapy was 8 days (IQR 6-15), longer than the median of 5 days reported in a recent cohort employing a standardised culture-guided approach in which ertapenem was discontinued once blood cultures had been negative for 48 hours. [17] Shorter, protocol-driven courses may be sufficient to achieve sterilisation while reducing the risk of resistant organism selection, a concern supported by the numerically higher rate of multi-resistant organism acquisition in combination-treated patients (11.5% vs 3.9%, P=0.15), a signal that warrants prospective evaluation.

text.text: This study has several important limitations.
Treatment allocation was not randomised, and confounding by indication is likely given the preferential use of combination therapy in more refractory and complex cases.

While the matched cohort design partially accounted for confounding in the primary analysis, no adjustment for confounders was made for secondary outcomes including 90-day mortality; these results should therefore be interpreted with this caveat in mind.

The combination-treated cohort was managed predominantly from 2021 onwards, whereas comparators were drawn from the full ten-year study period; improvements in standard of care over this interval may have differentially influenced outcomes.
All 26 combination-treated patients during their first episode were managed at a single centre, limiting generalisability.
The small exposed group constrains statistical power, and heterogeneity in dosing, timing, and source control strategies may have further confounded results.

This underscores a fundamental limitation of retrospective salvage therapy evaluations: without randomisation, spontaneous bacteraemia resolution cannot be excluded as an alternative explanation for the observed culture clearance.
Sex was not analysed as independent predictor of outcome; this represents a limitation to the generalisability of findings given the observed imbalance in sex distribution between groups.
This study has several notable strengths.

The cohort comprises 288 episodes of persistent MSSA bacteraemia accrued across two Queensland tertiary hospitals over a ten-year study period, representing one of the largest reported cohorts of this syndrome.

The matched cohort design, in which comparators were required to remain bacteraemic on the corresponding matched bacteraemia day and share key prognostic characteristics including age group, comorbidity burden, and presence of major metastatic foci, substantially mitigates confounding by illness severity.

The use of all eligible comparators without a fixed matching ratio, and the application of cluster-robust standard errors in the Cox regression model, further strengthens the validity of the primary analysis.
Together, these methodological features represent a meaningful advance over prior uncontrolled case series describing salvage combination therapy for persistent MSSA bacteraemia.

Cefazolin-ertapenem combination therapy was associated with accelerated blood culture sterilisation in persistent MSSA bacteraemia, representing the first matched comparative evidence for this strategy.

The present findings add to a growing body of observational evidence supporting this combination, but randomised evaluation is needed to establish whether accelerated clearance translates into improvements in mortality and relapse.
The ongoing SNAP trial, which includes a dedicated cefazolin-ertapenem arm (NCT04886284), will be particularly informative in this regard.
Future research should additionally evaluate optimal combination duration and patient-level predictors of treatment response.

text.text: Muscle toxicity was defined as a creatine kinase (CK) elevation greater than the upper limit of normal, or clinically documented myopathy, where daptomycin formed part of the treatment regimen.

Central nervous system toxicity was subcategorised as drug-attributable delirium, defined by clinical documentation in the medical record in the absence of an infective or metabolic aetiology, or new-onset seizure occurring during the treatment period without a prior seizure history or alternative precipitant.

Gastrointestinal toxicity included new diarrhoea attributed to antibiotic use, as well as Clostridioides difficile infection confirmed by toxin enzyme immunoassay or nucleic acid amplification testing within 90 days of antibiotic commencement.

Hypersensitivity reactions were defined as any immune-mediated response to an antimicrobial agent, including urticaria, angioedema, bronchospasm, or anaphylaxis, as documented by the treating clinician.
Cutaneous reactions encompassed drug-attributable rash of any morphology not meeting criteria for hypersensitivity.

Immunosuppression was defined as the presence of any of the following: chronic kidney disease, Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection, diabetes mellitus (type 1 or type 2), medication-related immunosuppression (see below) or disease-related immunosuppression (see below).

Medication-related immunosuppression was defined as current or recent use of any of the following agents: tumour necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α) antagonists; interleukin-6 (IL-6) antagonists (including tocilizumab); leflunomide; methotrexate; kinase inhibitors (including imatinib and ibrutinib); calcineurin inhibitors (ciclosporin and tacrolimus); mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibitors (sirolimus and everolimus); azathioprine; mycophenolate; cytotoxic chemotherapy; corticosteroids at a dose of ≥20 mg prednisolone equivalent per day for ≥3 weeks; anti-CD52 monoclonal antibody therapy (alemtuzumab); anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody therapy (rituximab); proteasome inhibitors (bortezomib and carfilzomib); or thalidomide analogues (lenalidomide, thalidomide, and pomalidomide).

Disease-related immunosuppression was defined as the presence of any of the following: an established autoimmune or inflammatory condition requiring ongoing medical management; active solid organ malignancy, excluding non-melanoma skin cancer; haematological malignancy, regardless of treatment status; or a primary immunodeficiency disorder of systemic significance.
Metastatic foci of infection were identified from clinical documentation, imaging, and 454 microbiological records, and categorised by anatomical site as follows.
Endocarditis was 455 classified as native valve endocarditis or prosthetic valve endocarditis, based on modified 456 Duke criteria.
Cases in which endocarditis status could not be determined from available 457 records were classified as unknown.

Bone and joint infection were subcategorised as native 458 joint infection, prosthetic joint infection, infection involving multiple joints, osteomyelitis 459 without joint involvement, or combined osteomyelitis with native joint infection.
Cases in 460 which bone or joint involvement could not be determined were classified as unknown.
Skin 461 and soft tissue infection was recorded as present or absent, with cases in which this could not 462 be determined classified as unknown.

CNS metastatic foci were defined as microbiologically 463 or radiologically confirmed infection at any intracranial or intraspinal site, and subcategorised 464 as brain abscess, cerebral emboli, epidural abscess, or combined cerebral and epidural 465 disease.
Cases in which CNS involvement could not be determined were classified as 466 unknown.
